purpose: Deferasirox is used to remove extra iron from your body that has built up because of repeated blood transfusions. Too much iron in your body can damage your heart, liver, and other organs. This medicine helps your body get rid of that extra iron safely through your stool and urine.
how_it_works: Think of deferasirox like a magnet for iron — it travels through your bloodstream and binds tightly to the excess iron floating around in your body. Once it grabs onto the iron, it forms a package that your body can then pass out through your digestive system. This process helps prevent iron from building up and causing damage to your vital organs.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or stomach pain are the most common side effects. You might also notice a skin rash or headache. Some people have changes in their urine color or mild hearing or vision changes. Taking the tablet form (Jadenu) with a small amount of food can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medication can affect your kidneys and liver, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to monitor how these organs are working. Tell your doctor right away if you notice decreased urination, swelling, yellowing of your skin or eyes, or severe stomach pain. It can also affect your hearing and vision, so report any changes right away. Avoid taking it with aluminum-containing antacids. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is about 14 to 20 mg per kilogram of your body weight once a day. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your iron levels and how your kidneys are working. Jadenu tablets can be swallowed whole with water or apple juice, while Exjade tablets are dissolved in water or juice and drunk right away, ideally at the same time each day, at least 30 minutes before eating.
